newsitem.title: NORWAY: Aker RGI unit to merge with Danish group.
newsitem.headline: Aker RGI unit to merge with Danish group.

text.p: Norway's Aker RGI said on Wednesday its subsidiary, Stord International as (SI), was to merge with Denmark's Atlas Industries A/S under the name Atlas Stord as.

The new company will be the world's leading supplier of equipment for fish and bone meal production, freeze drying, sugar processing, sludge drying and the alcohol and edible oil industries, Aker said in a statement.

The merger will be accomplished through the purchase of 45 percent of SI by Danish insurance company Pen-Sam for 56 million Norwegian crowns ($8.6 million). The deal prices SI as a whole at 125 million crowns compared with a book value for shareholders' equity of 75 million crowns, Aker said.
Aker RGI purchased 55 percent of Atlas Industries in September, 1996. The merged company will by owned 55 percent by Aker RGI and 45 percent by Pen-Sam.
Aker said the transaction will yield it a small accounting gain.
Atlas Stord will have annual revenues of around 600 million crowns and 550 employees.
